notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.20_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.20.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.20.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **A friend's profile, behind their name.** Who somebody is, the servers
  they publish and the ones you could invite them into used to sit above the
  conversation — so opening a friend put a list of servers, and two "Join"
  buttons meaning different things, between you and the last thing anybody
  said. A conversation is now only the conversation. The rest opens as a
  dialog from their name, or from a Profile item on the right-click menu in
  either friends list, and it covers the window rather than the chat.

- **The tray menu, on Windows and macOS, does what the Linux one does.** It
  offered "Friends" and "Exit Ruze"; the Linux tray has long carried a
  status picker and, during a call, the channel you are in with mute and
  leave beside it. All of it is there now: Online, Away and Busy as
  checkmarks — exactly one is ever true, which is what a radio group would
  have drawn anyway — and, only while there is a call to describe, its
  server and channel, a "Mute microphone" checkmark, and a way out.

  The item says what is true rather than what clicking it would do, because
  the tray is read precisely when the window is not in front of you. For the
  same reason the icon's tooltip now names the call, so "am I still in it"
  is answerable without a click.

  What made this hard is that only the Linux tray rebuilds its menu when a
  host asks for it; everywhere else the menu is an object the icon holds and
  nothing re-reads it. So it is rebuilt in full wherever the state it shows
  moves — on the main thread, since the items are native objects — and the
  two trays now run the same handlers, so they cannot drift apart in what
  the same item does.

### Fixed

- **A message that arrives while you are watching the conversation.** An
  entry names its content by hash and travels ahead of it, so a message that
  has just landed usually cannot be read for another moment. Those were
  dropped, on the reasoning that the next read of the conversation would
  pick them up — but a conversation on screen is never read again, only
  appended to, so what was dropped was not shown at all until the window
  happened to be opened afresh. An invitation is exactly the message you
  send to somebody who is looking at the conversation.

  They are held until the content lands now, and released when it does.
  Bounded, so content that never arrives cannot accumulate for the session;
  anything evicted is still in the document and comes back on the next read.

- **A window that stopped repainting while it caught up.** Joining a server,
  or opening one that was busy while this device was away, reconciles the
  missed history as one event per message — and each one copied the
  channel's list, re-sorted it and re-rendered every message on screen. A
  thousand arriving at once was a window that stopped drawing until it
  finished. What arrives together is applied together now: one update per
  channel however many came, with a ceiling so that a very long catch-up
  still shows progress as it goes rather than everything at the end.

- **Joining a server from the friends window.** Clicking one there tells the
  main window to show it, but that window had never heard of a server just
  joined in the other one — so the rail came up without it, and on a first
  join the whole window sat on the "join a server" screen, which is the one
  thing somebody who has just joined a server should not be looking at. The
  list is re-read before the server is selected.

- **The tray's mute checkmark after muting from the window.** The two show
  the same state, and the tray is redrawn rather than re-read, so it went on
  saying whatever had been true when the menu was last built.
